questions.text:
The heights of adult males in New Zealand are normally distributed with a mean of 177 cm and a standard deviation of 7.5 cm.

(i) Find the probability that a randomly selected adult male is taller than 185 cm.
(ii) Find the probability that a randomly selected adult male is between 170 cm and 190 cm.

A clothing company wants to manufacture shirts that fit the middle 90% of adult males.

(i) Find the range of heights that the shirts should be designed for.
(ii) What percentage of the male population would not be catered for by shirts of these sizes?
questions.markingGuide: Merit: (i) Middle 90% means 5% in each tail. z = ±1.645. Lower: 177 - 1.645 × 7.5 = 177 - 12.34 = 164.7 cm. Upper: 177 + 1.645 × 7.5 = 177 + 12.34 = 189.3 cm. Shirts should fit males between approximately 164.7 cm and 189.3 cm. (ii) 10% of the male population would not be catered for — 5% too short and 5% too tall.

questions.text:
A bus arrives at a bus stop every 15 minutes. The waiting time for a passenger who arrives at random follows a uniform distribution on the interval [0, 15] minutes.

(i) Write down the probability density function for the waiting time.
(ii) Find the expected waiting time and the standard deviation of the waiting time.
(iii) Find the probability that a passenger waits more than 10 minutes.

The time between earthquakes of magnitude 5.0 or greater in the Canterbury region can be modelled by an exponential distribution with a mean of 18 months.

(i) Find the probability that the next earthquake of this magnitude occurs within 12 months.
(ii) Given that 12 months have already passed without such an earthquake, find the probability of waiting at least another 12 months.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: (i) λ = 1/18. P(X ≤ 12) = 1 - e^(-12/18) = 1 - e^(-2/3) = 1 - 0.5134 = 0.4866. Merit: (ii) By the memoryless property of the exponential distribution, P(X > 24 | X > 12) = P(X > 12) = e^(-12/18) = e^(-2/3) = 0.5134. The probability of waiting another 12 months is the same regardless of how long we've already waited. This is the key property of the exponential distribution.

questions.text:
The random variable X has the probability density function:

f(x) = kx(4 - x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4
f(x) = 0 otherwise

(i) Find the value of k.
(ii) Find E(X).
(iii) Find P(X > 3).

The weights of packets of rice are normally distributed with a mean of 1.02 kg and a standard deviation of 0.03 kg. Packets are labelled as containing 1 kg of rice.

(i) Find the probability that a randomly selected packet weighs less than the labelled weight.
(ii) The manufacturer wants no more than 1% of packets to be underweight. To what value should the mean weight be set, assuming the standard deviation stays at 0.03 kg?
